summary.motive: Force man-coverage defenders into crossed releases that convert into a two-man rub, freeing a vertical behind single-high coverage.
summary.keyDefender: Free Safety (last line in man free)
summary.whyItWorks: Crossed releases make defenders trail through each other's lanes, and the far-side go routes strip the safety of any help he might offer to the rub side.
summary.failureMode: Corners jam both releases apart before they can cross, or the robber collision-calls the switch and jumps the outside climber.

beats.title: 1. The Switch Release
beats.text: X slams an inside release while H bursts outside behind him, exchanging lanes before either stem develops. Both defenders are forced to open in opposite directions.

beats.title: 2. Converting to Verticals
beats.text: Both receivers convert upfield simultaneously. The corner is dragged inside by the slam while the nickel trails through the crossing traffic — a natural rub neither can fight.

beats.title: 3. The Single-High Conflict
beats.text: The right-side go routes pin the free safety and hold the robber. The two left climbers attack the middle hole from opposite shoulders with no help coming.

beats.title: 4. The Throw to the Winner
beats.text: The quarterback delivers to whichever climber wins leverage. The outside release is live because the nickel is trailing — H stacks him and runs free behind the defense.

relations.tell: The releases cross below four yards before either stem develops — a true double-vertical keeps both receivers on parallel outside tracks.
